name: Managing Instance Security
apex: Administrator-level guide covering instance-wide controls: login lockout rules, public file upload, IP allow-listing, instance proxy, SSL/HTTPS enforcement, RESTful access, session rejoin, workspace isolation by hostname, session timeout, password reuse history, RESTful services.
attributes: Maximum Session Idle Time in Seconds
workflow: Instance administrator sets these once in APEX Administration Services; they cascade to every workspace unless overridden.
relevance: Multi-tenant Oracle instance admin has no Paddock analogue; Clerk already provides session length/idle timeout, Cloudflare already forces HTTPS, and there is no per-workspace hostname isolation to manage.

name: Configuring Instance Settings
apex: Instance-wide setup: automation level for creating new workspaces (manual/request/automatic), SMTP email, storage limits, and SSL wallets for outbound calls.
attributes: delete uploaded files after N days
workflow: Instance admin picks provisioning mode and email/storage settings once for the whole install.
relevance: Workspace self-service provisioning and wallets are Oracle-instance concerns; Paddock has one deployment with env-var secrets, no workspace signup flow.

name: Configuring Workspace Purge Settings
apex: Lets an instance admin auto-delete workspaces that have been inactive past a threshold, to reclaim storage and keep performance up.
workflow: Admin sets a days-inactive threshold; APEX purges qualifying workspaces automatically.
relevance: No equivalent concept; Paddock is one app, not a farm of tenant workspaces to prune.

name: Workspace to Schema Assignments
apex: Instance admins map each workspace to one or more database schemas so a workspace's developers can build against those schemas' objects.
workflow: Admin assigns schemas to a workspace at creation or later.
relevance: Paddock has one Supabase project/schema; there is no per-tenant schema routing to configure.

name: Managing Component Availability
apex: Workspace admins can restrict which developers may use App Builder, Team Development, SQL Workshop, or PL/SQL editing, e.g. letting someone run SQL but not build apps.
workflow: Admin toggles per-user rights on the Set Workspace Preferences / user account page.
relevance: If Paddock ever has more than one admin account, gating which designer areas (Data, Components, Health) a given account can reach is the same pattern as APEX's per-tool rights.

name: Integrating with Oracle BI Publisher
apex: Recommends running BI Publisher report printing over SSL and pointing APEX's Report Server URL at the HTTPS endpoint via a wallet.
workflow: Admin configures BI Publisher's HTTPS URL and wallet once for report printing.
relevance: Paddock has no BI Publisher-style report/PDF printing engine.

name: Runtime Environment
apex: A stripped APEX install that can run applications but exposes no App Builder, SQL Workshop, or other dev UI, reducing production attack surface.
workflow: Admin installs the runtime variant on production hosts and deploys exported apps into it; development stays on a separate full install.
relevance: Validates Paddock's existing design (designer routes gated behind Clerk role + isProductionWorker) and suggests going further: keep the designer's JS/routes out of the public bundle entirely, not just auth-gated, to shrink attack surface and Worker size.

name: Enabling Network Services (ACLs)
apex: Oracle Database requires an explicit network ACL grant before PL/SQL can send mail, call web services, or reach external print servers, blocking arbitrary outbound calls by default.
workflow: DBA grants a named ACL to the APEX schema for specific hosts/ports before that outbound feature works.
relevance: Same SSRF concern applies if Paddock ever lets an admin type in an arbitrary external URL (custom feed, webhook): allow-list destination hosts rather than fetching anything supplied.
skip_for_web: Cloudflare Workers allow outbound fetch by default; no DB ACL layer, but the allow-list principle still applies to any user-supplied URL feature.

name: Understanding Developer Security Best Practices
apex: Table-of-contents page pointing to the developer-facing security topics: password items, at-risk items, session state security, XSS protection, URL tampering, CSP, file upload security.
relevance: Overview page only; substance is captured under each linked topic's own notes.

name: Items of Type Password
apex: A page item type that masks input on screen and offers settings to avoid ever persisting the typed value to the database.
attributes: Session State Storage: Per Request (Memory Only)
Store value encrypted in session state
workflow: Developer sets Storage to Per Request for sensitive fields, or turns on encrypted storage if the value must persist across requests.
relevance: Direct pattern for any password or secret input Paddock Developer exposes, such as a data-source credential field: never echo it back, avoid persisting plaintext, and encrypt at rest if it must be stored.

name: Identifying At-Risk Password Items
apex: Two cross-application reports, Security Profiles and Password Items, that flag password items which save state unencrypted, so a developer can find and fix them across every app in the workspace.
workflow: Developer runs the report periodically and fixes any item flagged At Risk by turning on encryption or switching to memory-only storage.
relevance: Useful audit habit in principle, but Paddock has no stock of password-type form items to sweep; a one-off code search covers the same ground.
skip_for_web: No multi-app inventory of password fields to audit.

name: Session State and Security
apex: APEX stores all session state server-side in database tables, not client-side, because that is more secure and avoids holding a live DB connection per user between requests.
attributes: Store value encrypted in session state
workflow: Developer clears unneeded session values with clear-cache processes or directives and encrypts any sensitive value that must persist.
relevance: Different execution model entirely: Paddock is stateless per-request in a Worker with Clerk-issued session cookies and DB rows, not a page-item session-state table to clear or encrypt field by field.

name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Protection
apex: APEX system of automatic and manual output escaping that stops attacker-supplied text from being rendered as executable HTML or script in regions, reports, and form items.
workflow: Rule of thumb for developers: never emit a session-state value without escaping unless the item is a designated safe type that was itself escaped on input.
relevance: Same rule applies wherever Paddock designer lets an operator author free-form text or HTML for a page block: escape by default, and only allow raw markup through an explicit, clearly labelled safe or raw HTML block type.
skip_for_web: React and JSX escape by default so most of APEX manual-escaping mechanics are moot; only the raw-HTML opt-in principle carries over.

name: Report Column Escaping (#COLUMN!X#)
apex: Extended column notation for report HTML Expressions that lets a developer choose exactly how a value is escaped: HTML, attribute, JavaScript, raw (unescaped), or HTML-stripped.
workflow: Developer picks the suffix matching the output context instead of concatenating raw HTML into the query, so escaping is not bypassed.
relevance: Templating-language escaping suffixes are APEX-specific syntax; a React or TypeScript designer expresses the same idea as typed escape helpers per context, not string suffixes.

name: Restricting Characters Entered on an Item
apex: A page-item Security attribute that blocklists or allowlists specific characters, such as HTML brackets, quotes, PL/SQL comment markers, and newlines, from ever being saved to session state.
attributes: Blocklist reserved chars and PL/SQL comment marker
workflow: Developer sets the restriction on a field; APEX rejects the submission with an error if the input violates it.
relevance: Same idea as Paddock adding server-side input validation or character allowlists on any free-text designer field, such as component names or slugs, rather than relying on escaping alone.

name: Session State Protection
apex: A built-in checksum system that stops attackers from tampering with f?p= URLs to alter session state or program flow they should not be able to reach.
workflow: Developer enables it once per app in Shared Components, then sets a protection level per page and per item, either via a wizard or individually in Page Designer.
relevance: Confirms the general web principle Paddock already needs: never let a client-supplied URL or query param set privileged app state without a server-side check tied to the authenticated session.
skip_for_web: The f?p= URL and checksum mechanism itself is APEX-specific; Paddock equivalent is normal server-side auth and CSRF checks on any mutating route.

name: Session State Protection checksum levels
apex: Four graduated levels controlling how an item value may be set via URL: Unrestricted, checksum required at Application, User, or Session level, or Restricted so the browser can never set it.
attributes: Restricted - May not be set from browser
workflow: Developer picks the strictest level that still lets the legitimate navigation flow work, per item or per page.
relevance: The four-tier checksum scheme is tightly coupled to APEX stateful URL syntax; Paddock has no f?p= link format to checksum.

name: Page Access Protection
apex: A page-level setting controlling whether the page can be requested via URL at all, and if so whether Request, Clear-Cache, or Name-Value arguments require a checksum.
workflow: Developer sets this per page in Page Designer Security group; No URL Access still allows internal Branch-to-Page navigation.
relevance: Maps to routing and middleware concerns Paddock already solves with Next.js route groups and Clerk middleware, not a page attribute to configure per page.

name: Content Security Policy (CSP)
apex: A web security standard delivered via HTTP response headers that tells the browser which origins scripts, styles, images, and other resources may load from, blocking everything else, which mitigates XSS and data-injection attacks.
workflow: Developer enables CSP at the application level under Security Attributes and picks enforce vs report-only while testing.
relevance: Paddock (Next.js on Cloudflare) should ship its own CSP header; the enforce vs report-only rollout pattern is directly reusable, and CSP is standard web platform behavior, not APEX-proprietary.

name: Types of CSP Violations
apex: Catalog of what CSP blocks once enabled: inline script tags without a nonce, inline style attributes or tags, inline event-handler attributes like onclick, and external resources loaded from an origin not in the allow-list.
workflow: Developer checks the browser console for these violation messages when adopting CSP and fixes each occurrence.
relevance: Same violation categories apply verbatim to any Next.js app; Paddock would hit the same onclick or inline-style breakage in old code when it turns on CSP, so this is a ready-made checklist.

name: Cryptographic Nonce for CSP
apex: A random, per-request value the server places in both the CSP header and an inline script or style tag attribute; only tags carrying the matching nonce are allowed to execute, so legitimate inline code still runs while injected code is blocked.
workflow: Server generates a fresh nonce per request; developer adds a nonce attribute to any inline script or style tag that must run.
relevance: Directly reusable: Next.js middleware can generate a per-request nonce and inject it the same way, letting Paddock keep any necessary inline script while still enforcing a strict CSP.

name: CSP Header Directives
apex: The directive syntax that makes up a CSP header value, restricting each resource category to an explicit source list, for example default-src, object-src, img-src.
workflow: Developer writes the header value as a semicolon-separated list of directive-plus-allowed-sources pairs.
relevance: Standard CSP syntax, not APEX-specific; Paddock can copy this directive set nearly as-is as a starting policy: self plus nonce for scripts, block object and embed, allow data: images.

name: Best Practices for CSP Compliant Development
apex: Practical rollout advice: move inline scripts and styles to external files, use nonce substitution strings for the inline code that must stay, and test with browser devtools while iterating the policy before enforcing it.
workflow: Developer builds the policy in Report-Only mode, watches devtools for blocked-resource warnings, fixes or allow-lists each one, then switches to enforcing mode.
relevance: This is the rollout sequence Paddock should follow when it adds a CSP header: ship Report-Only first, clear console warnings, then enforce; directly actionable for the planned Security tab.

name: CSP Substitution Strings
apex: Four placeholder tokens APEX resolves per request when building CSP-compliant markup: the nonce value, a full nonce attribute, and a display:none helper for hiding content before load.
workflow: Developer drops these tokens into custom templates or HTML regions instead of hardcoding a nonce or inline style.
relevance: APEX template substitution syntax specifically; a Next.js equivalent is just template variables or props in the render function, not a distinct feature to copy.

name: Securing File Uploads
apex: Warns that APEX file-upload page items land in a shared instance-wide storage table (APEX_APPLICATION_FILES) that can be read without authentication by anyone who knows the file id, so sensitive uploads should go to a table you own or APEX_APPLICATION_TEMP_FILES instead.
workflow: Developer routes uploads to a workspace-owned table, or the temp-files view, so the page normal authorization checks also cover file access.
relevance: Same lesson applies to any Paddock file upload: never serve an uploaded asset from a globally-guessable, unauthenticated path; gate the serving route with the same auth check as the owning page.

name: Controlling Access to Applications, Pages, and Page Components
apex: Parent overview page for the Access Control feature; introduces the concept and links to the wizard, user management, and per-page authorization topics.
relevance: Table-of-contents page; substance captured in the child topics (Access Control wizard, Manage User Access, per-page schemes) noted separately.

name: Access Control (wizard-built RBAC)
apex: A one-click wizard that bolts role-based access control onto an app: an Access Control admin region, three roles (Administrator, Contributor, Reader) mapped to three privileges (Administration, Edit, View), matching authorization schemes built on APEX_ACL.HAS_USER_ROLE, a build option, and an ACCESS_CONTROL_SCOPE setting.
workflow: Developer runs the wizard once; it wires the roles, schemes, and admin UI together, then attaches the generated authorization schemes to whichever pages or components should be role-gated.
relevance: Concrete worked example of role-scoped designer access: three named roles, ready-made auth checks, and a UI to assign them, a strong template if Paddock adds collaborator roles beyond a single operator.

name: Any Authenticated User Access toggle
apex: A single On/Off setting deciding whether users authenticated to the app but absent from the access control list get baseline (Reader) access anyway, or are locked out until explicitly added.
attributes: Any authenticated user may access this application (On/Off)
workflow: An administrator flips this in the runtime Access Control admin page to choose open-baseline-access versus invite-only.
relevance: Same open-vs-invite-only decision Paddock would face if it adds a signed-in-but-unlisted-user tier, such as a future contributor role; worth copying as an explicit toggle rather than an implicit default.

name: Creating Access Control via Create Page Wizard
apex: The Create Page wizard flow (Features, Access Control) that generates the admin pages, starting page number, page group, and build option needed to add the feature to an existing app.
workflow: Developer runs Create Page, chooses Access Control, and answers a few placement questions; the wizard does the rest.
relevance: Wizard mechanics for generating APEX pages and build options; Paddock components are code, not generated pages, so there is no equivalent scaffolding step to mirror.

name: Manage User Access
apex: The admin screen for CRUD on the access control list: add a user by Username, Email, Role, bulk-add many usernames at once to one role, edit or lock an account, or delete a user.
workflow: Administrator opens Access Control on the app Administration page and manages who has which role from one table-style screen.
relevance: Directly transferable screen design for a future Paddock manage-collaborators admin page: one table, add or edit or lock or delete, bulk-add by list, matches how Clerk Organizations already models members plus roles.

name: Controlling Access for Pages and Page Components
apex: Six ready-made authorization schemes generated by the Access Control wizard that any page or component can select: three positive checks (Administration, Contribution, Reader Rights) and their three negated forms.
workflow: Developer edits a page or a region, button, or item and picks one of these six from its Authorization Scheme attribute to gate visibility by role.
relevance: Good UX pattern for Component Settings: expose role-gating as a simple named-scheme dropdown per component, including negated variants, rather than free-form boolean logic.

name: Removing a Wizard-Built Feature via Build Options
apex: Every wizard-generated feature is wrapped in a Build Option (Include or Exclude); flipping it to Exclude makes the APEX engine treat the feature and its components as if they do not exist, without deleting anything, and permanent removal means deleting the components then the build option.
workflow: Developer toggles the build option to soft-disable a feature for testing, or deletes its components first and the build option last to remove it for good.
relevance: Same idea as Paddock own feature-flag gate (GrowthBook, build_flags.yaml): a reversible Include or Exclude switch before committing to permanent deletion is good discipline for the designer own optional features.

name: Application Access Control (roles and user assignments)
apex: The lower-level role primitive behind Access Control: define named roles with a static identifier, then assign users to roles directly on the Application Access Control page, independent of the wizard-built pages.
workflow: Developer creates roles first, then adds a user-role assignment per user; roles can be copied or subscribed across applications like other shared components.
relevance: The export gotcha is the useful nugget: roles export and import with the app but user-to-role assignments do not, so every deploy needs a manual or scripted reseed step, the same class of problem Paddock already handles for seed or reference data.
skip_for_web: The role CRUD screens themselves are redundant with the Access Control wizard already noted; Clerk Organizations would hold the actual user-role data.

name: Establishing User Identity Through Authentication
apex: Parent overview page introducing authentication (username and password, certificates, or a secure key) and linking to the preconfigured schemes, creation, configuration, and reporting topics.
relevance: Table-of-contents page; Paddock has already standardized authentication on Clerk, which supersedes this entire APEX subsystem.

name: Preconfigured Authentication Schemes
apex: A gallery of built-in authentication methods a developer can pick when creating a scheme: Builder Extension Sign-in, Custom, Database Accounts, HTTP Header Variable, LDAP Directory, No Authentication (DAD), Open Door Credentials, APEX Accounts, Oracle AS SSO, SAML, and Social Sign-In.
workflow: Developer creates a scheme from the gallery, configures it, then clicks Make Current Scheme to activate it for the application.
relevance: Clerk already provides social sign-in, SAML, and its own account store as managed features; Paddock would configure these in the Clerk dashboard, not build APEX-style schemes.

name: Builder Extension Sign-in
apex: An authentication scheme that lets a user open a published Extension App from an existing APEX builder session without signing in again, gated by a workspace-level Allow Hosting Extensions setting.
workflow: Administrator enables extension hosting for the workspace; the extension app then trusts the current APEX session instead of prompting for credentials.
relevance: Single-sign-on between two Oracle-specific app types with no Paddock analogue, since Paddock has one app, not a builder-plus-hosted-extension pair.

name: Custom Authentication
apex: A from-scratch authentication scheme giving full control of the login form and session rules, used when built-in schemes cannot meet needs like activity auditing, session expiry limits, custom redirect logic, or a shared session across multiple applications.
workflow: Developer builds a login form and a PL/SQL authentication function, then wires it in as a Custom scheme.
relevance: Clerk is Paddock chosen custom-grade auth provider already; there is no reason to hand-roll a login form or session function.

name: Session Management Security (identity binding)
apex: APEX records the user identity at session creation and, on every request, checks the current authenticated identity still matches it, redirecting to a fresh session if not, which blocks both deliberate session-ID guessing and accidental reuse of a stale bookmarked session.
workflow: Enforced automatically once Custom Authentication is used; not a developer-configured attribute.
relevance: Confirms a general session-security property worth verifying in Paddock own session handling: a session ID or cookie should always be checked against the identity that created it, not just checked for validity.

name: Database Accounts
apex: Authenticates end users against real database schema accounts in the local database; a good fit only when one database account per named user is feasible.
workflow: Developer selects this scheme type when creating an authentication scheme.
relevance: Paddock has no per-user database accounts and would never want end users mapped to Supabase roles.

name: HTTP Header Variable Authentication
apex: Trusts a username the web server or an upstream SSO layer already validated and placed in a request header (default REMOTE_USER), re-verified every request or only after login.
workflow: Developer points the scheme at the header name the front-door server sets, and chooses how often APEX re-checks it matches the current session.
relevance: Same shape as trusting a Cloudflare Access identity header in front of a Worker; the Each Request versus After Login re-verification choice is a useful model if Paddock ever layers Access in front of the designer.

name: LDAP Directory Authentication
apex: Verifies a login-page username and password by binding to a corporate LDAP server with a constructed distinguished name.
workflow: Developer supplies the LDAP host, port, and DN pattern, optionally transforming the entered username first.
relevance: No enterprise directory to integrate with; Clerk is the single identity source for Paddock.

name: No Authentication (using DAD)
apex: Adopts the current database session user as the app user, relying on a web-server-level basic-auth challenge (mod_plsql DAD) to have already identified them.
workflow: Developer leaves Username blank to fall back to the database session user, or hardcodes a fixed username for prototyping.
relevance: Tied to mod_plsql and DAD web-server configuration with no Paddock counterpart; Clerk always identifies the user explicitly.

name: Oracle APEX Accounts
apex: Authenticates against APEX own built-in user repository; quick to stand up but Oracle explicitly advises against it in production, recommending a full external identity provider instead.
workflow: Developer picks this scheme for prototyping or small internal tools, not for production-facing apps.
relevance: Validates rather than informs a decision already made: Paddock chose an external identity provider (Clerk) instead of a homegrown account store, exactly as Oracle recommends here.

name: Oracle Application Server Single Sign-On Server
apex: Legacy delegation to Oracle AS 9iAS SSO as a registered partner application; Oracle itself now recommends SAML or Social Sign-In instead.
workflow: Only appears if the 9iAS SSO SDK is installed; developer registers the app as an SSO partner first.
relevance: Deprecated legacy protocol with no modern equivalent Paddock would ever adopt.

name: SAML Sign-In
apex: Delegates authentication to a SAML identity provider for enterprise single sign-on, requiring the Instance Administrator to configure it before any application can use it.
workflow: Administrator configures SAML at the instance level; developer then selects it as an application scheme.
relevance: Clerk already offers SAML SSO as a managed feature for enterprise customers if Paddock ever needs it; no reason to build the protocol handling.

name: Social Sign-In Verify Attributes check
apex: An option that rejects an OAuth or OpenID login if the identity provider marks the username-bearing attribute, such as email, as unverified, preventing an attacker from impersonating another user via an unverified claim.
workflow: Developer enables Verify Attributes whenever the username attribute could plausibly be attacker-supplied and unverified at the provider.
relevance: Universal OAuth lesson worth double-checking in Clerk configuration: never treat an unverified email or phone claim from a social login as a trusted user identifier.
skip_for_web: The rest of the Social Sign-In scheme, such as Discovery URL, callback URLs, and credential store, is superseded wholesale by Clerk managed social connections.

name: Authentication Scheme lifecycle (view, create, configure, activate, copy/subscribe, reports)
apex: The full CRUD lifecycle for an authentication scheme: view which one is current, create it from the gallery or by copying, configure login and post-logout and session-sharing hooks, activate with Make Current Scheme, copy or subscribe to reuse one from another application, and view its subscription and history reports.
workflow: Developer manages every authentication scheme through Shared Components, Security, Authentication Schemes using this same set of actions.
relevance: All superseded by Clerk, which owns sign-in configuration outside Paddock own codebase; the copy or subscribe across apps mechanic also does not apply since Paddock is one application.

name: Runtime Authentication Configuration Procedure
apex: A PL/SQL hook that runs at session start and can swap the active authentication scheme, substitute template values like a discovery URL, and set a tenant id, letting one application definition serve many tenants with different sign-in configurations resolved by request hostname.
workflow: Developer writes a procedure that inspects HTTP_HOST or similar and returns the right scheme name and substitution values for that tenant.
relevance: Solves multi-tenant SaaS auth, one app instance serving many customer domains; Paddock is single-tenant with a fixed Clerk configuration, so there is no per-request auth resolution to build.

name: Editing an Authorization Scheme (evaluation point caching)
apex: Lets a developer control how often an authorization scheme boolean check is re-evaluated and cached in the session: once per session, once per page view, once per component, or always with no caching, plus an API to force-clear the cached result.
workflow: Developer picks the loosest caching level that is still correct for the check, tightening it only if the authorization depends on state that changes within a session.
relevance: Directly useful caching model for Paddock role or permission checks in the designer: memoize an expensive Clerk role lookup at the right granularity instead of recomputing it on every component render, with an explicit invalidation path.

name: Copying or Subscribing to an Authorization Scheme
apex: Copies an authorization scheme from another application in the workspace, optionally keeping it linked to the source as a subscription that can later be refreshed.
workflow: Developer picks a source app and scheme, names the copy, and chooses whether to keep it subscribed.
relevance: Same cross-application shared-component subscription pattern already logged elsewhere; Paddock has one application so there is no second app to copy from.

name: Report Pages Without Authorization Schemes
apex: An audit report listing which pages in the application have no authorization scheme attached at all, alongside a companion report of pages that do, plus subscription, utilization, and history reports for authorization schemes.
workflow: Developer runs this report periodically to catch pages that were never given an access check.
relevance: Exactly the kind of audit Paddock planned Security tab or Health page should offer: a list of admin or designer routes with no role check attached, to catch an accidentally unprotected page before it ships.

name: Two Translation Methods: Application-Based vs Text-Message-Based
apex: APEX offers two ways to serve a multi-language app: Application-Based forks a full separate copy of the application per language kept in sync by re-running the translation steps after every change, while Text-Message-Based keeps one application and swaps out named text strings by session language.
workflow: Developer picks the method once on the Globalization page; Text-Message-Based is the lower-maintenance choice for an app that keeps evolving.
relevance: If Paddock ever needs multi-language content, this is the cautionary tale to copy the right half of: use a single-codebase, message-key i18n approach like next-intl and avoid anything resembling forking a whole separate app copy per locale.

name: Language Identification and Fallback Matching
apex: The application language can be resolved from a static primary-language setting, the browser Accept-Language, a stored user preference, an item, or the session; if the exact locale has no translation, APEX falls back from a full locale such as en-us to its base language en and finally to the primary language.
workflow: Developer chooses one resolution source for the whole app; APEX applies the exact-then-truncated-then-primary fallback automatically.
relevance: Standard, correct locale-resolution and fallback order that any future Paddock i18n work should copy rather than reinventing.

name: Marking Content as Translatable or Not
apex: Region titles are translatable by default and can be explicitly excluded (Exclude Title from Translation); templates are excluded by default since they should hold structure, not prose, and must be explicitly flagged Translatable to appear in the translation file.
workflow: Developer flips these switches to keep the generated translation file limited to real user-facing prose.
relevance: Same distinction Paddock content already needs if it ever adds locales: mark which frontmatter fields are translatable prose versus structural config, so a translation export does not choke on slugs, dates, or component keys.

name: Multibyte Language Support
apex: Running several languages such as Chinese and Japanese at once requires configuring the database with a character set that covers all of them, typically UTF8 or AL32UTF8.
workflow: Administrator sets the database character set before any multibyte translation work begins.
relevance: Modern web stacks (Next.js, Postgres, browsers) are UTF-8 by default; there is no character-set decision for Paddock to make.

name: Application Primary Language and Translation switch
apex: The Globalization page setting that names the source-of-truth language an app is authored in, and the on/off switch plus method choice that turns on translation support at all.
workflow: Developer sets the primary language once; all future edits are made in that language and propagated outward to translations.
relevance: Paddock has one authoring language; nothing to configure until multi-language is actually planned.
skip_for_web: Single-language site today, matches the task framing exactly.

name: XLIFF Export/Import Translation Workflow
apex: A seed-export-translate-import-publish pipeline: translatable text is seeded into a repository, exported as an XLIFF file (an open XML localization standard vendors support), translated externally, re-uploaded, and applied; incomplete translations fall back per-string to the primary language rather than failing.
workflow: Developer re-runs seed and export after every content change so the translation file stays in sync, then applies and publishes once translated text returns.
relevance: The per-string fallback-to-primary behavior during partial translation is the durable lesson: any future Paddock i18n pipeline should tolerate incomplete translations gracefully rather than blocking or showing blank text.
skip_for_web: XLIFF itself and the seed and publish mechanics are APEX-specific; a modern equivalent would use a JSON or YAML catalog and a service like Crowdin or Lokalise.

name: Convert to Text Messages Wizard
apex: A one-time bulk-conversion tool that scans an application and turns hardcoded translatable strings into named Text Messages, the prerequisite for the lower-maintenance Text-Message-Based translation method; it skips template directives, numeric text, and text already marked not-translatable.
workflow: Developer runs the wizard after building the app, reviews any exceptions it could not convert automatically, and re-runs it after adding new UI text.
relevance: Same shape as an automated i18n-extraction codemod, such as an i18n-ally or next-intl extractor, that finds hardcoded strings and replaces them with translation keys; worth adopting a similar tool-assisted extraction step if Paddock ever internationalizes.

name: Manually Editing a Translation (Translation Repository)
apex: A report and grid-edit screen over the seeded translation repository where a developer can hand-edit the translate-to text for any string, optionally propagating one correction to every occurrence of the same source string.
attributes: Update all occurrences of this string
workflow: Developer or translator edits strings directly in APEX instead of round-tripping through an XLIFF file, useful for small fixes.
relevance: A lightweight in-tool translation editor is nice but low priority versus a dedicated third-party TMS; not needed while Paddock ships one language.

name: Translating Default Reports (IR/IG)
apex: Only developer-saved Primary and Alternative default reports on interactive reports and grids are translatable (report name, filter and highlight names, chart axis labels, and IR/IG-specific labels); reports end users save themselves, public or private, are never translated.
workflow: Developer includes these in the normal seed, export, translate, publish cycle; anything a user personally saved is left in its original language.
relevance: Good scoping rule for any future Paddock i18n effort: translate what an editor curates and ships, never content or view preferences an end user generates themselves.

name: Translating Messages (overview)
apex: Parent overview page linking to when to translate PL/SQL-generated text, translating APEX own internal runtime messages, and the Text Messages management screen.
relevance: Table-of-contents page; substance captured in the child topics noted separately.

name: About Translating Messages
apex: Identifies two situations needing message translation: an app with PL/SQL-generated HTML, or an app targeting a language outside the ten APEX ships pre-translated in, which needs its own report messages translated too.
relevance: Both triggers are specific to APEX generating its own UI chrome and PL/SQL output; Paddock UI strings live in its own React components, not framework-generated HTML.

name: APEX_LANG.MESSAGE API
apex: A runtime function that looks up a named Translatable Message by key and returns it in the current session language, for use inside PL/SQL procedures, functions, triggers, or packages that generate their own HTML.
workflow: Developer defines the message once by name, then calls the API wherever that text is generated in code instead of hardcoding it.
relevance: Exactly the t(key) pattern from next-intl or i18next; validates that any Paddock server-generated string, such as emails or error messages, destined for i18n should go through a keyed lookup function, never a hardcoded literal.

name: Translating Messages Used Internally by APEX
apex: APEX ships its own runtime UI pre-translated into 34 languages; targeting any other language means the developer must supply translations for APEX own internal messages too, not just their application text.
workflow: Developer checks whether the target language is in the pre-translated list before committing to translate the framework own runtime strings as well.
relevance: Paddock has no vendored framework UI chrome to translate; every string in the app is already first-party and would go through a Paddock-owned i18n catalog if that is ever built.

name: Internal Messages Requiring Translation (reference list)
apex: A reference table of roughly 150 core APEX runtime message keys and their English text, such as dialog buttons, validation errors, and relative-time strings, that must be translated for any language outside the pre-translated set.
workflow: Translator works through this list key by key when supporting a new language.
relevance: Pure reference data for translating Oracle vendored UI strings; nothing conceptual beyond the message-catalog pattern already captured elsewhere.

name: Interactive Grid Messages Requiring Translation (reference list)
apex: A much larger reference table, over 400 keys, of Interactive Grid specific runtime strings covering toolbar actions, filter operators, relative date phrases, chart and aggregate dialogs, and grid help text.
workflow: Translator works through this list when supporting a new language for apps that use interactive grids.
relevance: Pure reference data tied to a component Paddock does not have; no concept here beyond the message-catalog pattern already logged.

name: Isolating Workspaces (Allow Hostnames)
apex: Forces different workspaces onto different hostnames in the URL so the browser same-origin policy itself blocks one from attacking another, rather than relying only on server-side checks.
workflow: Administrator assigns a distinct hostname per workspace that needs isolation from the others on the same instance.
relevance: Validates Paddock existing structural isolation: prod, testing., and paris. already run on separate subdomains, which is the same same-origin defense described here.

name: Require HTTPS enforcement levels
apex: Three levels for forcing HTTPS: Always (every app including builder), Development and Administration only, or Application specific (left to each app own setting).
workflow: Administrator picks one level instance-wide; the web server must still be configured for HTTPS separately.
relevance: Cloudflare already forces HTTPS at the edge for every route; there is no equivalent tiered choice to make.

name: Restricting Password Reuse
apex: An instance-wide setting (PASSWORD_HISTORY_DAYS) that blocks a user from reusing a password they used within the last N days, checked against stored password hashes.
workflow: A DBA runs an APEX_INSTANCE_ADMIN.SET_PARAMETER call once to set or disable the reuse window.
relevance: Password lifecycle policy is Clerk responsibility for any account using password sign-in; Paddock has no local password store to police.

name: Allow Public File Upload (instance kill switch)
apex: An instance-wide attribute that controls whether unauthenticated, anonymous users can upload files at all in any application that offers file upload.
workflow: Administrator turns this off to guarantee no app on the instance can accept anonymous uploads, regardless of per-app settings.
relevance: Same instance-level kill switch is worth having if Paddock ever adds any public-facing upload surface, such as a comment attachment: a single flag to disable all anonymous uploads instantly.

name: Restrict Access by IP Address
apex: An instance-wide, comma-delimited allow-list of IP addresses permitted to reach the APEX instance at all.
workflow: Administrator enters the allowed IP list once to lock the whole instance down to known networks.
relevance: Cloudflare WAF IP Access Rules provide the same capability; worth turning on for the Paddock Developer designer routes as defense-in-depth beyond the Clerk role check.

name: Instance Proxy for outbound HTTP
apex: Configures the whole APEX instance to route all outbound HTTP traffic, web services, URL regions, and report printing through a single proxy, overriding any app-level proxy settings.
workflow: Administrator sets this once when the network requires all egress to go through a corporate proxy.
relevance: Cloudflare Workers egress does not route through a configurable forward proxy in this way; no equivalent setting exists for Paddock.

name: RESTful Access and Services opt-in flags
apex: Two separate instance or workspace toggles: one allows exposing report regions as RESTful services, the other allows developers to create and edit ORDS-mapped RESTful Web Services at all.
workflow: Administrator must explicitly enable both categories before a developer can expose any data as a REST endpoint.
relevance: Paddock API routes are code-defined in Next.js already; there is no separate platform-level enablement flag needed before a route can exist.

name: Restricted session state protection level
apex: A page-item or application-item protection level meaning the value can never be set from the browser at all, via URL or POSTDATA, no matter what; only internal processes and computations may set it.
attributes: Restricted - May not be set from browser
workflow: Developer applies this to any item that must only ever be assigned by server-side logic, never by user input.
relevance: Directly reusable design rule: any Paddock designer field that should only ever be computed or set internally, such as a derived id or a role flag, should be structurally unwritable by client input, not just validated.

name: Session State Protection Settings Summary
apex: A single rollup report on the Session State Protection wizard showing the protection level currently set for every page, page item, and application item, so a developer can spot gaps at a glance.
attributes: Page Level Session State Protection Summary
Page Item Session State Protection Summary
workflow: Developer expands these regions before changing any settings to see what is already configured.
relevance: Same audit-dashboard idea as the earlier Report Pages Without Authorization Schemes finding: Paddock planned Security tab should show one rollup of which routes and fields have which protection level, not require checking each individually.

name: Login Throttle on Failed Attempts
apex: APEX built-in authentication flow includes a login throttle that tells a user to wait a counted-down number of seconds before retrying after failed sign-in attempts, evidenced by the internal message key APEX.AUTHENTICATION.LOGIN_THROTTLE.COUNTER.
workflow: Enforced automatically by the built-in authentication flow; not a separate developer-configured attribute in the docs reviewed.
relevance: Worth explicitly verifying Clerk enforces equivalent brute-force login throttling for Paddock sign-in, since this is a baseline expectation for any auth system.

name: Open Door Credentials
apex: A built-in login page that accepts any username with no real credential check, meant purely for use during application development.
workflow: Developer selects this scheme temporarily during early development, then swaps it for a real scheme before going live.
relevance: Paddock local dev already uses real Clerk test accounts; no need for a fake, no-check login mode.

name: Enabling CSP in an Application (attribute location)
apex: CSP headers are set as a Browser Security, HTTP Response Header attribute reached either from Edit Application Definition, Security tab, or from Shared Components, Security Attributes.
workflow: Developer opens either path to the same Security Attributes screen and pastes in the header value.
relevance: Confirms CSP belongs in a dedicated Security settings surface, not scattered per-page; Paddock planned Security tab should be the single place its CSP header value lives and is edited.

name: Document Direction (RTL support)
apex: A per-language attribute on the Define Application Languages mapping that sets text direction to Language Default, Left-To-Right, or Right-To-Left.
workflow: Developer sets this once per target language when mapping it, typically Right-To-Left for Arabic or Hebrew.
relevance: If Paddock ever adds an RTL language, this flags the requirement early: layout and CSS need a dir-aware or logical-properties approach, not just translated strings.

name: Translatable Message Shortcuts (HTML vs JavaScript-escaped)
apex: Two shortcut flavors for referencing a translated message inline: a plain Message shortcut for HTML contexts, and a JavaScript Escaped Single Quotes variant that safely embeds the same text inside a JS string literal.
attributes: Message with JavaScript Escaped Single Quotes
workflow: Developer picks the shortcut matching where the translated text will be emitted, HTML markup or a JS literal.
relevance: Same context-aware escaping discipline already flagged for CSP and XSS: any translation or templating system Paddock builds needs distinct HTML-safe versus JS-safe output helpers, not one generic string interpolation.

name: Escape Special Characters (form items)
apex: A per-item Security attribute, default On, controlling whether a form item value is HTML-escaped when redisplayed to the browser; turning it Off is only safe if the field intentionally holds trusted markup.
workflow: Developer leaves this On for ordinary data entry fields and only disables it for a field deliberately used to hold pre-sanitized HTML.
relevance: Direct, concrete rule for Paddock form fields and designer inputs: escape by default, and treat any raw-HTML-allowed field as an explicit, reviewed exception.

name: Form Auto Complete = Off for password pages
apex: A page-level attribute that stops the browser from offering to autofill or remember values on a page containing password items.
workflow: Developer sets this to Off on any page with a password item.
relevance: Simple, directly copyable HTML attribute (autocomplete off) for any Paddock form field holding a credential or secret, reducing accidental browser-side exposure.

name: How Translated Applications Are Rendered
apex: Application-Based translation renders an entirely separate, forked application definition per language; Text-Message-Based renders the same single application, substituting text at runtime, falling back to the primary language for any missing message.
workflow: Developer picking Application-Based must remember it is a genuinely separate app copy, not a view over the same one.
relevance: Concrete mechanism behind the earlier method-comparison finding: reinforces that a forked-copy approach means real drift risk, while single-codebase substitution stays consistent by construction.

name: Continuous Re-seeding Requirement
apex: Seeding translatable text must be re-run every time the primary-language application changes, or the translation repository and the exported files drift out of sync with the live app.
workflow: Developer re-runs seed and export as a routine step after any content or UI change, not a one-time setup task.
relevance: Operational lesson for any future Paddock i18n pipeline: string extraction has to be a repeated, ideally automated step tied to every content change, not a one-off migration.

name: Export All vs Only New or Updated Elements
apex: The XLIFF export screen lets a developer export every translatable element or only the ones that are new or changed since the last export, avoiding re-translating unchanged strings.
attributes: Export: only new or updated elements
workflow: Developer chooses the delta-only export for routine updates and the full export only for the first pass or a full audit.
relevance: Same delta-sync idea used by modern translation-management tools like Crowdin or Lokalise; worth building into any future Paddock i18n pipeline so translators are never re-shown unchanged strings.

name: Static Identifier vs display Name (roles)
apex: An access control role has both a human-editable Name and a separate Static Identifier meant to be referenced from code, so renaming the display name later does not break anything that checks the role programmatically.
workflow: Developer sets both when creating a role: a friendly Name for the UI and a stable Static Identifier for authorization-scheme code.
relevance: Good general pattern already worth confirming Paddock follows for its own component types and roles: a stable machine key separate from the human-editable label, so renaming in the UI never breaks stored references.

name: Authentication Scheme Program Hooks
apex: An existing authentication scheme exposes configurable hooks beyond credential checking, such as login processing, a post-logout URL, and session-sharing behavior, that a developer can wire custom logic into.
workflow: Developer edits the current scheme attributes to add logic that should run at login or logout time.
relevance: Direct parallel to Clerk webhooks (user.created, session.created): Paddock should lean on those events for any post-login sync work, such as creating a Supabase profile row, rather than inventing a separate hook system.

name: Declarative Attributes Are Auto-Translatable
apex: Field labels, region headings, and page header text are declarative attributes captured by App Builder and automatically included in the translation file, unlike text generated imperatively by PL/SQL code which needs explicit handling.
workflow: Developer relies on App Builder to surface these for translation automatically; only code-generated text needs a manual API call.
relevance: Validates a Paddock architecture principle: keep user-facing text in declarative content or config files wherever possible, since that is what stays analyzable and swappable, rather than building strings in code.

name: Dynamic Translation Text Strings
apex: A translate-from string, language code, and translate-to string triple used to translate database-driven values at runtime, such as a list of values populated by a query, retrievable via the APEX_LANG.LANG API.
workflow: Developer defines the from/to pairs per language and calls the API wherever the raw database value would otherwise display untranslated.
relevance: Paddock content values (series names, driver names) live in curated files rather than needing a runtime key-value translation lookup table; low priority until real multi-language demand exists.

name: Translation Drift Risk (Application-Based)
apex: The Application-Based method explicitly warns that any change to the primary application, a refreshed theme, a new page item, an edited title, requires manually repeating the seed-through-publish steps or the translated copy silently falls out of sync.
workflow: Developer must remember to re-run the whole pipeline after every primary-app edit; nothing detects drift automatically.
relevance: Concrete cautionary data point reinforcing why a forked-per-locale approach is the wrong model to copy: no built-in staleness detection means drift is silent until a user notices.

name: Creating an Authentication Scheme
apex: The Shared Components screen where a developer creates a new authentication scheme, either based on a pre-configured gallery entry or as a copy of an existing one, naming it and picking a Scheme Type.
attributes: Create Scheme: Based on a pre-configured scheme
Create Scheme: As a copy of an existing scheme
workflow: Developer creates the scheme here, but it is inactive until separately made current.
relevance: Pure APEX CRUD screen for a subsystem Clerk replaces entirely.

name: Changing the Authentication Scheme (Make Current Scheme)
apex: A new authentication scheme is inactive by default; the developer must open it and click Make Current Scheme before the application actually uses it to authenticate.
workflow: Developer creates and configures a scheme first, tests it is correct, then activates it with this one action.
relevance: An explicit activate-when-ready step is reasonable general practice but not a feature Paddock needs to build, since Clerk configuration changes apply directly.

name: Copying or Subscribing to an Authentication Scheme
apex: Copies an authentication scheme from another application in the workspace, optionally keeping it linked as a live subscription that can later be refreshed or unsubscribed; the companion Subscribing page offers the same link-and-refresh flow directly from the scheme edit page.
workflow: Developer picks a source application and scheme, then chooses a one-time copy versus a live subscription that stays in sync.
relevance: Cross-application shared-component reuse has no target in a single-application codebase like Paddock.

name: Viewing Authentication Scheme Reports
apex: Two report tabs on the Authentication Schemes page: Subscription, showing which schemes are subscribed from elsewhere, and History, showing recent modifications to authentication items in the application.
workflow: Developer checks these tabs to audit where a scheme came from or what changed recently.
relevance: Same audit-trail idea Paddock already gets from git history on any Clerk configuration-as-code; no separate in-app report needed.

name: Subscribing to an Authentication Scheme
apex: Links an authentication scheme to a master copy in another application so it can be refreshed with that master's changes on demand, set up directly from the scheme own Create/Edit page rather than via a copy wizard.
workflow: Developer selects a master application and scheme in the Subscription region, then applies to link them.
relevance: Same cross-app shared-component subscription pattern noted repeatedly; no second application exists in Paddock to subscribe from.
